$comment: Config lab exercises. An exercise is solved when the file has no errors or warnings (tips are fine) and every requirement - a JMESPath query over the analyser's facts - is true. `solution` is a reference answer; the tests check that it is clean.

exercises.title: Fix a broken release pipeline
exercises.description: This Azure Pipelines file never gets past validation. Fix every error and warning, keeping the Build, Test and Deploy stages in that order.
exercises.file:
trigger:
  - main

stages:
  - stage: Build
    jobs:
      - job: Compile
        steps:
          - task: UseDotNet
            inputs:
              version: 8.x
          - script: dotnet build -c Release
            displayName: Build

  - stage: Test
    dependson: Biuld
    jobs:
      - job: Unit
        pool:
          vmImage: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - script: dotnet test

  - stage: Deploy
    dependsOn: Tset
    jobs:
      - job: Release
        pool:
          vmImage: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - script: echo deploying
exercises.solution:
trigger:
  - main

pool:
  vmImage: ubuntu-latest

stages:
  - stage: Build
    jobs:
      - job: Compile
        steps:
          - task: UseDotNet@2
            inputs:
              version: 8.x
          - script: dotnet build -c Release
            displayName: Build

  - stage: Test
    dependsOn: Build
    jobs:
      - job: Unit
        steps:
          - script: dotnet test

  - stage: Deploy
    dependsOn: Test
    jobs:
      - job: Release
        steps:
          - script: echo deploying

requirements.description: The Build, Test and Deploy stages are still there, in that order
Test depends on Build, and Deploy on Test

exercises.title: A proper deployment job
exercises.description: The Deploy stage uses a plain job and keeps the database password in the YAML. Turn it into a deployment job targeting the `production` environment (with a runOnce strategy), and get the password out of the file.
exercises.file:
trigger:
  branches:
    include: [main]

pool:
  vmImage: ubuntu-latest

variables:
  appName: shop-api
  dbPassword: S3cr3t-Pa55!

stages:
  - stage: Build
    jobs:
      - job: Build
        steps:
          - script: dotnet publish -c Release -o $(Build.ArtifactStagingDirectory)
          - task: PublishPipelineArtifact@1
            inputs:
              artifact: drop

  - stage: Deploy
    jobs:
      - job: Deploy
        steps:
          - task: AzureWebApp@1
            inputs:
              appName: $(appName)
exercises.solution:
trigger:
  branches:
    include: [main]

pool:
  vmImage: ubuntu-latest

variables:
  - group: shop-secrets
  - name: appName
    value: shop-api

stages:
  - stage: Build
    jobs:
      - job: Build
        steps:
          - script: dotnet publish -c Release -o $(Build.ArtifactStagingDirectory)
          - task: PublishPipelineArtifact@1
            inputs:
              targetPath: $(Build.ArtifactStagingDirectory)
              artifact: drop

  - stage: Deploy
    jobs:
      - deployment: Deploy
        environment: production
        strategy:
          runOnce:
            deploy:
              steps:
                - task: AzureWebApp@1
                  inputs:
                    azureSubscription: shop-prod-connection
                    appName: $(appName)

requirements.description: Build and Deploy stages are still there
The Deploy stage still deploys a web app

exercises.title: A workflow that never runs
exercises.description: This GitHub Actions workflow has a typo in its trigger, a job without a runner, a step that tries to be two things and a `needs` that points nowhere. Make it valid, keeping the build, test and deploy jobs.
exercises.file:
name: CI

onn:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install and build
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        run: npm ci && npm run build

  test:
    needs: biuld
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: npm test

  deploy:
    needs: [build, test]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: ./deploy.sh
exercises.solution:
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
      - name: Install and build
        run: npm ci && npm run build

  test:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: npm test

  deploy:
    needs: [build, test]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: ./deploy.sh

requirements.description: build, test and deploy jobs are still there
deploy still waits for build and test

exercises.title: Harden a release workflow
exercises.description: This release workflow works - and leaks. It pins an action to a branch, runs with the default token permissions, prints a secret and uses the retired `::set-output`. Fix the errors and warnings without losing the release job.
exercises.file:
name: Release

on:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@master
      - name: Version
        id: version
        run: echo "::set-output name=tag::v1.$GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER"
      - name: Publish
        run: |
          echo "Token is ${{ secrets.PUBLISH_TOKEN }}"
          ./publish.sh
exercises.solution:
name: Release

on:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Version
        id: version
        run: echo "tag=v1.$GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Publish
        run: ./publish.sh
        env:
          PUBLISH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PUBLISH_TOKEN }}

requirements.description: The release job is still there
It still has its three steps

exercises.title: Slim down a Node.js image
exercises.description: This image works, but it is huge, runs as root, rebuilds every dependency on every change and uses whatever node:latest is today. Fix every error and warning.
exercises.file:
FROM node:latest

RUN apt-get update
RUN apt-get install -y curl

WORKDIR /app
COPY . .
RUN npm install
RUN npm run build

EXPOSE 8080
CMD npm start
exercises.solution:
FROM node:20 AS build
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY . .
RUN npm run build

FROM node:20-alpine
RUN apk add --no-cache curl
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build /app/dist ./dist
COPY --from=build /app/node_modules ./node_modules
USER node
EXPOSE 8080
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s CMD wget -qO- http://localhost:8080/health || exit 1
CMD ["node", "dist/server.js"]

requirements.description: It still starts the app with CMD or ENTRYPOINT
It still exposes port 8080

exercises.title: Secrets in a .NET image
exercises.description: Someone baked the database connection string into this .NET API image, and the image ships the full SDK. Get the secret out, build in a separate stage, and fix the rest.
exercises.file:
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:8.0
ENV ConnectionStrings__Default="Server=sql-prod;User=app;Password=Pa55word!"
ARG NUGET_TOKEN
WORKDIR /src
ADD . .
RUN dotnet restore
RUN dotnet publish -c Release -o /app
WORKDIR /app
EXPOSE 8080
ENTRYPOINT dotnet Shop.Api.dll
exercises.solution:
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:8.0 AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY *.csproj ./
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=nuget_token dotnet restore
COPY . .
RUN dotnet publish -c Release -o /app

FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:8.0
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build /app .
USER $APP_UID
EXPOSE 8080
HEALTHCHECK CMD curl -f http://localhost:8080/health || exit 1
ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "Shop.Api.dll"]

requirements.description: It still runs Shop.Api with an ENTRYPOINT
It still exposes port 8080

exercises.title: A Python worker done right
exercises.description: This worker image pipes an installer script into a shell, uses sudo, keeps the pip cache and runs as root. Fix every error and warning.
exercises.file:
FROM python:3.12-slim
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y sudo curl
RUN curl -sSL https://install.example.com/agent.sh | sh
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN sudo pip install -r requirements.txt
COPY . .
CMD ["python", "worker.py"]
exercises.solution:
FROM python:3.12-slim
RUN apt-get update \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
COPY . .
RUN useradd --create-home --uid 10001 worker
USER worker
HEALTHCHECK CMD python -c "import worker; worker.health()" || exit 1
CMD ["python", "worker.py"]

requirements.description: It still runs worker.py
It is still based on python:3.12-slim

exercises.title: A tiny Go image
exercises.description: Build this Go service in one stage and ship only the binary, on a distroless base, as a non-root user.
exercises.file:
FROM golang
WORKDIR /src
COPY . .
RUN go mod download
RUN go build -o /bin/api ./cmd/api
EXPOSE 8080
ENTRYPOINT ["/bin/api"]
exercises.solution:
FROM golang:1.23 AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY go.* ./
RUN go mod download
COPY . .
RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o /bin/api ./cmd/api

FROM gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot
COPY --from=build /bin/api /bin/api
EXPOSE 8080
HEALTHCHECK NONE
ENTRYPOINT ["/bin/api"]

requirements.description: It still runs /bin/api
It now has a separate build stage

exercises.title: A production-ready Deployment
exercises.description: This Deployment would be rejected - its selector does not match its pods - and even then it would run one copy of :latest with no limits and no probes. Fix every error and warning.
exercises.file:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: shop-api
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: shop-api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: shop
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: api
          image: myregistry.azurecr.io/shop-api:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
exercises.solution:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: shop-api
  namespace: shop
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: shop-api
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: shop-api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: shop-api
    spec:
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
      containers:
        - name: api
          image: myregistry.azurecr.io/shop-api:1.4.2
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 100m
              memory: 128Mi
            limits:
              memory: 256Mi
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health/ready
              port: 8080
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health/live
              port: 8080
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            capabilities:
              drop: ["ALL"]

requirements.description: It is still the shop-api Deployment
It still runs the shop-api image

exercises.title: Lock down a node agent
exercises.description: This log collector was given far too much power: privileged, on the host network, as root, with the whole of /var mounted from the node. Make it pass - it only needs to read /var/log.
exercises.file:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: log-agent
  namespace: monitoring
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: log-agent
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: log-agent
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: log-agent
    spec:
      hostNetwork: true
      containers:
        - name: agent
          image: fluent/fluent-bit:3.1
          securityContext:
            privileged: true
            runAsUser: 0
          resources:
            requests: { cpu: 50m, memory: 64Mi }
            limits: { memory: 128Mi }
          readinessProbe: { httpGet: { path: /api/v1/health, port: 2020 } }
          livenessProbe: { httpGet: { path: /api/v1/health, port: 2020 } }
          volumeMounts:
            - name: var
              mountPath: /var
      volumes:
        - name: var
          hostPath:
            path: /var
exercises.solution:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: log-agent
  namespace: monitoring
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: log-agent
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: log-agent
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: log-agent
    spec:
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 10001
      containers:
        - name: agent
          image: fluent/fluent-bit:3.1
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            capabilities: { drop: ["ALL"] }
          resources:
            requests: { cpu: 50m, memory: 64Mi }
            limits: { memory: 128Mi }
          readinessProbe: { httpGet: { path: /api/v1/health, port: 2020 } }
          livenessProbe: { httpGet: { path: /api/v1/health, port: 2020 } }
          volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /var/log
              readOnly: true
      volumes:
        - name: logs
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: node-logs

requirements.description: It is still the log-agent DaemonSet

exercises.title: A safe nightly job
exercises.description: A nightly CronJob that exports orders. It uses :latest, has no resource limits and runs as root. Fix every error and warning (batch jobs do not need probes).
exercises.file:
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: export-orders
  namespace: shop
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: export-orders
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        metadata:
          labels:
            app.kubernetes.io/name: export-orders
        spec:
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          containers:
            - name: export
              image: myregistry.azurecr.io/exporter
              args: ["--since", "24h"]
exercises.solution:
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: export-orders
  namespace: shop
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: export-orders
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        metadata:
          labels:
            app.kubernetes.io/name: export-orders
        spec:
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
          containers:
            - name: export
              image: myregistry.azurecr.io/exporter:2.0.1
              args: ["--since", "24h"]
              resources:
                requests: { cpu: 250m, memory: 256Mi }
                limits: { memory: 512Mi }
              securityContext:
                allowPrivilegeEscalation: false

requirements.description: It is still the export-orders CronJob
